messages:
jamal: quick question — for new Dedicated customers do we route spans to per-customer datasets or use a shared export pool with tagging?
alex: leaning per-customer datasets for isolation and retention control, but cost and infra complexity go up.
maya: agree on isolation for compliance customers. For standard customers shared pool + strict tagging + RBAC should be fine.
gina: UX concern: product wants a simple switch in console to opt into isolation. We need routing to respect that flag immediately, not as a delayed rollout.
jamal: technical tradeoff: per-customer datasets mean separate exporter instances or routing keys at ingest. Which is less invasive?
alex: two options: (1) have collector inspect resource.attributes["redwood.org_id"] and rewrite exporter.endpoint -> /export/{org} (2) keep single exporter and set export.headers X-Org: {org} and let downstream writer split.
maya: option 2 is easier to roll out but puts trust in downstream exporters to enforce RBAC. Option 1 centralizes enforcement but collector config explosion.
gina: console needs to show per-org quota usage and retention settings. If we rely on downstream split, metrics might be delayed.
ops-bot: @jamal created ticket INF-1428 for per-org export routing prototype.
sre-oncall: if we do per-org datasets, we must add fallback rules: when org-specific writer is down, route to a degraded shared buffer with TTL and alert.
jamal: good point. Fallback should preserve deletion/retention semantics — we can't mix-retain different retention windows in same shard.
alex: proposal: route by header X-Org to primary writer; if writer returns 503 or auth error, collector marks org in degraded mode and switches to fallback queue with metadata tag "degraded-org:{org_id}" and short retention (48h) until operator resolves.
maya: that lets us keep a shared pool but still separate retention by tagging and enforcement during export. But enforcement will be eventual, and customers may notice shorter retention.
gina: product wants canary rollout: start with 5 pilot orgs, console toggle, and show clear banner when org is in degraded-mode.
jamal: about RBAC — should we mint short-lived per-org exporter tokens at ingest time? That avoids trusting headers from collectors.
alex: we could leverage our control plane PKI, mint tokens scoped to writers. Collector exchanges org_id for writer token via control-plane endpoint. Slight latency on first request. Cache tokens per collector-worker.
sre-oncall: make sure token minting has rate limits. Attack surface if collectors get compromised.
maya: operational note: telemetry SDKs sometimes don't set resource attributes reliably (k8s envs). We need a fallback mapping based on API key -> org_id in ingest layer.
jamal: agreed. So final API for routing: prefer resource.attributes.org, else fall back to API-key lookup, else tag as "unknown" and route to shared noisy pool.
gina: console UX: add tooltip "unknown orgs are routed to shared pool and subject to sampling".
ops-bot: INF-1428 updated with collector-prototype link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/320
jamal: small config sketch for the collector (for the record):
```
receivers:
  otlp:
processors:
  batch:
  attribute:
    actions:
      - key: redwood.org_id
        action: delete
exporters:
  redwood_writer:
    endpoint: https://write.redwood.ai/export
    headers: {"x-org": "${REDWOOD_ORG}"}
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, attribute]
      exporters: [redwood_writer]
```
jamal: (above is pseudo) — collectors will set REDWOOD_ORG from resource or api-key lookup.
alex: next steps: implement token minting MVP + fallback queue prototype. Pilot with 3 customers.
maya: I'll coordinate test corp and compliance validation.
gina: I'll spec console toggles and degraded-mode banner copy.
sre-oncall: I'll draft runbook for degraded-mode and fallback drain.
jamal: thanks all — let's sync briefly tomorrow. :thumbsup:
